summary: feat(concur): sync --resources expenses iterates reports and reconciles deletions; scan-duplicates refuses a never-synced store and ignores rows without a report
reason: sync --resources expenses was unimplemented, yet expenses scan-duplicates still printed duplicate groups built from stale local rows that had no report_id. A user relying on it to avoid double-filing got a misleading answer.
validated_outcome: Unit tests cover per-report sync, a failing report mid-run, refusal on a never-synced store, ignoring empty report_id rows, and a real cross-report duplicate. Live against a real tenant (read-only API calls): sync fetched 268 expenses from the newest 100 reports and scan-duplicates reported the data age. After review: a dry-run sync no longer writes sync state; each fetched report's missing expenses are dropped in the same transaction as the upsert (skipped under --no-prune or when any item in the listing could not be read). Live: dry-run left the sync timestamp unchanged and a real sync updated it.
